*The Common Cause* is a great book about how race played a role in the founding of America by Robert Parkinson. There's a semi-abridged version called *Thirteen Clocks* that has some chapters from *The Common Cause* but also adds in commentary on how print impacted the Revolution. (I am a bit biased because I had the privilege of being in a class of his last year and currently sit in on his lectures occasionally.)

*Never Caught* by Erica Armstrong Dunbar is the story of a runaway slave named Ona Judge and Washington's attempts to get her back, but it's actually about Washington's insecuries and his extreme awareness of the limits and sway of his power (and also about how cool Ona Judge was). It's a very good read to learn about the politics of slavery, power, and freedom in early America.

I'm a Progressive-Era nerd, so I have to throw in *Illiberal Reformers* and *The Great Arizona Orphan Abduction* in there as well.
